answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity deposit of scarce compute that cannot be shared across keys. An agent answers by proving hardware time with a receipt bound to one public key. A new key starts on an empty terrace with no standing, paying the full deposit before its first reply is scored. Many keys do not help: costs add linearly while trust is earned from scratch on each, so clones stay at zero. Each extra identity adds one deposit plus compute to lift it. A sybil reply needs the same sonnet of proof as an honest one, with no discount. At zenith, capture costs as much as honest work.
